trace.code: char *pw_password = authctxt->valid ? shadow_pw(pw) : pw->pw_passwd;  // locked/key-only account -> shadow hash "*"
if (authctxt->valid && pw_password[0] && pw_password[1]) salt = pw_password;  // "*" has pw_password[1]=='\0', so salt stays NULL
encrypted_password = xcrypt(password, salt);  // NULL salt -> pick_salt() from another account's $6$ hash
crypted = crypt(password, salt);  // musl crypt(): >256-byte key -> returns "*" (KEY_MAX error sentinel)
return encrypted_password != NULL && strcmp(encrypted_password, pw_password) == 0;  // "*" == "*" -> ACCEPT

ret = encrypted_password != NULL && salt != NULL && strlen(pw_password) >= MIN_PASSWORD_HASH_LEN && strcmp(encrypted_password, pw_password) == 0;  // 1-byte "*" hash fails strlen>=4 and salt!=NULL -> REJECT

preconditions: sshd built against musl libc with PAM disabled (e.g. Alpine Linux default openssh-server package), OpenSSH < 10.6p2
A target account whose shadow password field is the locked marker "*" (key-only account, or a service account with no password set)
At least one other local account with a $5$ (SHA-256) or $6$ (SHA-512) password hash, so pick_salt() finds a salt
Attacker supplies any password of 257..1024 bytes (MAX_PASSWORD_LEN) over SSH

evidence.vulnerable_version: OpenSSH < 10.6p2 on Linux with musl libc and PAM disabled (e.g. Alpine Linux openssh 3.16-3.24, and any musl build without PAM)
evidence.observed_result: Real OpenSSH sys_auth_passwd()/xcrypt()/pick_salt()/shadow_pw() (verbatim from auth-passwd.c and openbsd-compat/xcrypt.c) compiled with x86_64-linux-musl-gcc -static and run against real musl crypt(). musl crypt() returns "*" for a 300-byte key with a $5$/$6$ salt (KEY_MAX=256 error sentinel), so the vulnerable strcmp("*","*") accepts a 300-byte password for the locked '*' account (return 1). The fixed function (MIN_PASSWORD_HASH_LEN>=4 and salt!=NULL guards) rejects the same input (return 0).

real_exploit.target: openssh/openssh-portable auth-passwd.c sys_auth_passwd() @ 3c6ec4c (pre-10.6p2) + openbsd-compat/xcrypt.c xcrypt()/pick_salt()/shadow_pw() driving musl libc crypt()
real_exploit.backend: real OpenSSH functions (copied verbatim from the pinned commits) compiled natively against real musl libc (x86_64-linux-musl-gcc -static); getpwent()/getspnam() stubbed with a controlled /etc/shadow (account 'locked' = "*", account 'root' = valid $6$ hash)
real_exploit.demonstrated: A 300-byte SSH password authenticates as the locked/key-only 'locked' account on musl: crypt(300-byte key, $6$salt) returns the 1-byte "*" error sentinel, which equals the account's stored "*" hash, so the vulnerable sys_auth_passwd() returns 1 (ACCEPT). The 10.6p2-fixed sys_auth_passwd() rejects the identical input (returns 0) because strlen("*") < MIN_PASSWORD_HASH_LEN(4) and no salt was derived.
